assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Policy thresholds (650/600 credit scores) appear in a dedicated policy column (e.g. 'Credit threshold') separate from the applicant's actual credit score column.
assertions.evidence: The table shows 'Credit Score' column with values like 650, 651, 600, 601, but no separate 'Credit threshold' column. Thresholds are only mentioned in @Description text, not as explicit table columns.

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms (e.g. '70', '650', 'APPROVED') — not abstract codes.
assertions.evidence: Values include concrete numbers (64, 650, 651, 65, 600, 601, 90, 700, 40) and domain terms (REJECTED, APPROVED, PENDING_REVIEW).

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior at lower threshold', 'Missing income') — not outcomes ('Approved', 'Rejected').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names like 'Non-senior, just below threshold', 'At senior cutoff, above lowered threshold', 'Above threshold, unknown income' describe conditions, not outcomes.

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Age', 'Credit score', 'Stable income', 'Decision?') — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: Columns are named 'Age', 'Credit Score', 'Stable Income', 'Result?' — all business language, no code identifiers.

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Result?, Result?

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 2 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 2 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table.
assertions.evidence: Two @TableTest methods: 'appliesAgeBasedCreditScoreThreshold' and 'determinesResultFromIncomeStatus', each addressing a distinct concern.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations.
assertions.evidence: First table has 6 rows covering age boundaries (64, 65, 90) and threshold boundaries (650, 651, 600, 601). Second table has 5 rows covering income states (true, false, null) and threshold crossing.

assertions.text: Age boundary policy, credit score categorisation, and income status are separated into distinct @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: appliesAgeBasedCreditScoreThreshold isolates age/credit rules (income fixed true); determinesResultFromIncomeStatus isolates income handling (age fixed at 40).

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description text do not restate values the table already shows.
assertions.evidence: First @Description states 'Stable income is held true throughout every row' — this is a fixed constant not shown as a column, so it's acceptable. However, the second @Description states 'age is fixed at a representative non-senior value here' without naming the value, which is acceptable. No redundant restatement of column values in scenario names detected.

assertions.text: The effect of stable income on the outcome is visible from table rows with two rows differing in stable-income column while holding credit score and age equal.
assertions.evidence: Second table rows 1-3 all have creditScore=700, age=40 (fixed), but differ in Stable Income (true→APPROVED, false→REJECTED, null→PENDING_REVIEW), showing income's effect on result.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable. No table has all identical expectations, all expectations copying input cells, or would be satisfied by ignoring inputs.
assertions.evidence: First table: expectations vary (REJECTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, APPROVED) and don't copy input cells. Second table: expectations vary (APPROVED, REJECTED, PENDING_REVIEW, REJECTED, REJECTED) and don't copy inputs. Both tables require reading inputs to determine outputs.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 shows age thresholds (64→650, 65→600) and outcomes as concrete values. Table 2 shows income states (true/false/null) mapped to results. Column headers and cell values are self-contained.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName states what the code under test does, not an external fact.
assertions.evidence: "appliesAgeBasedCreditScoreThreshold" and "determinesResultFromIncomeStatus" describe evaluator actions. Removing "evaluator" leaves no true statement about regulations or domain facts alone.
